name: Dihydropteridine Reductase Deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Biochemical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for DHPR Deficiency

criteria.description: Reduced dihydropteridine reductase enzyme activity in fibroblasts or blood cells
Elevated blood phenylalanine levels detected on newborn screening
Identification of pathogenic variants in the QDPR gene
Low cerebrospinal fluid levels of biogenic amines (dopamine and serotonin metabolites)
Presence of neurological symptoms such as developmental delay and movement disorders

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of hyperphenylalaninemia, reduced DHPR enzyme activity, and pathogenic QDPR gene variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires biochemical confirmation and genetic testing; early diagnosis critical for treatment.

searchTerms: global delay in growth and skills

laboratory: Reduced dihydropteridine reductase enzyme activity in blood or fibroblasts
Low cerebrospinal fluid levels of homovanillic acid (HVA) and 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid (5-HIAA)
imaging: MRI may show cerebral atrophy or delayed myelination
other: Response to tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) and neurotransmitter precursor therapy

distinguishingFeatures: Responds to dietary phenylalanine restriction alone
Deficiency of GTP cyclohydrolase I enzyme
Different pattern of neurotransmitter metabolite abnormalities

redFlags: Severe hyperphenylalaninemia detected on newborn screening
Refractory seizures and movement disorders despite standard treatment
references: Blau N, Thöny B, Cotton RJ, et al. Dihydropteridine reductase deficiency. In: GeneReviews® [Internet]. University of Washington, Seattle; 2020.
